subject: Confirming data exclusion from model training and retention TTL questions
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finovate.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal+privacy@finovate.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2029 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Data exclusion from model training + TTL semantics

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time today. Procurement and our privacy team had a few follow-ups after the security questionnaire — mostly to confirm the exact language we can present to our stakeholders. Can you confirm the following in writing so we can close the item on our side?

1) Will Redwood ever use our Customer Content (prompts, files, responses) to train or improve your underlying models? If there are exceptions (e.g., opt-in, aggregated telemetry), please describe them.

2) What are the retention windows for: request logs, full request payloads (including inputs/outputs), backups/snapshots, and debug traces? Are there different windows for Hosted API versus Dedicated / Private deployments?

3) What is the deletion pathway once we request data removal? How do you handle backups and snapshots that may contain echoes of customer content?

4) For procurement — can you provide an attestation letter or a signed statement we can attach to the contract that says Redwood doesn’t train models on our data (or call out the exact scope if there are caveats)?

We’ve attached our internal checklist to show the items they need answered. If it helps, legal+privacy@finovate.com is cc’d to iterate on contract language.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product Security
Finovate Labs

Attachments: Finovate_Data_Use_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with procurement questions)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finovate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2029 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data exclusion from model training + TTL semantics

Hi Samira — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a few implementation details you can paste into procurement: 

1) Do we train on Customer Content? No — Redwood does not use Customer Content to train or update our foundation models. That includes prompts, uploaded files, outputs, and conversation history sent to our hosted inference endpoint. We can provide a signed attestation for procurement (see attachment).

Caveat: We may collect limited operational telemetry (API error rates, latencies, anonymized token counts) for product improvement and capacity planning. That telemetry is aggregated and contains no customer prompt/response text. If you require zero telemetry collection for certain workloads, Dedicated or Private deployment options allow controlling telemetry forwarding; we can add contractual controls in the DPA.

2) Retention windows (typical defaults, Hosted API):
- Request logs (metadata: timestamps, client IP hash, model used): 30 days
- Full request payloads (inputs + outputs retained for debugging): default 90 days; customers can shorten this via config or choose Dedicated/Private to keep payloads in their environment
- Backups / snapshots (infrequent infra snapshots that may incidentally contain data): retained for up to 365 days for disaster recovery; we tombstone and rotate snapshots and have a documented deletion/extract process
- Debug traces / core dumps: retained up to 90 days and only pulled for specific incident investigations; access is logged and limited to authorized engineers

Note: For Dedicated and Private, retention defaults differ because data can remain in your VPC or on-prem; we offer contractual retention SLAs in those deployments.

3) Deletion pathway:
- Primary data deletion: on request, we delete Customer Content from live storage and mark the record as deleted (tombstone) within 48 hours.
- Snapshot/backups: we maintain an audit-runbook for purging content from backups during the next maintenance window; for Hosted customers, this typically completes within 90–180 days depending on snapshot cadence. We will commit to a clear RTO/RPO and deletion timeline in the contract if required.
- Evidence: we can produce a deletion certificate with timestamps and internal ticket IDs for audit purposes.

4) Attestation and contract language:
- I’ve attached our standard attestation (redwood-data-exclusion-attestation.pdf) and a retention matrix (redwood-data-retention-matrix.xlsx) for your legal team. If you want specific contract text, we propose the following clause: 

  "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or improve its models or algorithms. Redwood may collect aggregated, non-textual telemetry for operational purposes; such telemetry will not include Customer Content."

If that wording needs to be stronger or more granular (e.g., explicitly call out backups, debug snapshots, telemetry buckets), Mina in legal can provide the signed attestation and add precise DPA language. Happy to jump on a short call to align.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-exclusion-attestation.pdf; redwood-data-retention-matrix.xlsx

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finovate.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2029 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: Data exclusion from model training + TTL semantics

Hi Samira — looping in legal to close this out. Per Karthik’s note (quoted below), we can provide a formal signed attestation and incorporate specific retention windows into the DPA. Suggested next steps:

- I can provide an executed attestation letter that states: "Redwood does not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any of Redwood's foundation models, inference models, or associated model artifacts. Customer Content will not be added to any training datasets."
- If you need an exception for aggregated telemetry, we will include an explicit carve-out that describes categories of telemetry and an opt-out mechanism for Dedicated/Private customers.
- For Hosted customers, we will commit to: 30-day metadata retention, 90-day full payload retention default, 365-day backup retention with documented purge windows. We can shorten any of these windows in contract.

If that addresses procurement, I’ll attach the signed attestation and propose a short 30-min call with your privacy team to finalize contract language.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
